correctness.rationale: Complete n>=4 proof: every mixed pair initially observes all but at most two vertices and forces both; a pure set with r>=2 initially observes the opposite shore, and a force is possible exactly when at most two same-shore vertices remain. Singletons stall. This iff proves both polynomials and complete inclusion-minimality. The TAR proof shows all mixed sets of budget >=3 lie in one component, identifies the exact pure isolated sets at budget n-2, and connects all of them by one opposite token at budget n-1; n=4 is handled separately. A standalone direct forcing simulator for n=4..8 checks all 87296 vertex subsets, both coefficient arrays, 350 minimal sets, and 25 TAR component computations.

value.rationale: Power domination is a classical PMU-placement model and token-addition/removal reconfiguration formalizes changes between feasible monitoring placements. This two-shore family has two sharply separated kinds of inclusion-minimal placements; the exact census yields a nonmonotone connectivity phase for every n>=6, with an exact linear-size stable threshold n-1 and 1+n(n-1) components at the intervening budget. It is a natural complete infinite-family classification/refinement of known broad bounds, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
